title: Files and Directories
subtitle: touch, mkdir, cp, mv, rm — creating, copying, moving, and deleting
author: KERNAL Team

content.code:
# Create an empty file (or update its timestamp if it exists)
touch notes.txt
touch index.html style.css app.js   # create multiple files

# Create a directory
mkdir projects
mkdir -p projects/myapp/src         # -p creates parent dirs as needed
mkdir -p {images,css,js}            # brace expansion: creates 3 dirs

# Check what was created
ls -la

# Copy a file
cp README.md README.md.bak          # copy to same directory with new name
cp notes.txt ~/Documents/           # copy to a different directory
cp -r src/ backup/                  # -r: copy directory recursively

# Move (also used for renaming)
mv oldname.txt newname.txt          # rename
mv notes.txt ~/Documents/           # move to different directory
mv *.log /var/log/archive/          # move all .log files

# Move multiple files into a directory
mv file1.txt file2.txt destination/

content.text: Deleting files — be careful, no Trash

content.code:
# Delete a file
rm notes.txt

# Delete multiple files
rm file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt

# Delete a directory and its contents
rm -r myproject/         # recursive delete
rm -rf node_modules/     # force + recursive (no prompts)

# Safer: interactive delete (asks before each file)
rm -i *.log

# Delete an empty directory
rmdir empty_folder/

content.text: rm is permanent — there is no Trash. There is no undo. rm -rf / would delete everything on the system. Always double-check the path before running rm -rf. Consider using trash-cli (a safe alternative) or adding an alias: alias rm='rm -i' in your .bashrc.

questions.question: You run: mv report.pdf reports/. What happens?
options: report.pdf is copied into reports/ and the original remains
report.pdf is moved into the reports/ directory (original location is empty)
Error — mv cannot move files into directories
questions.explanation: mv moves the file — the original is gone, and reports/report.pdf now exists. Unlike cp (which copies and keeps the original), mv transfers the file. The trailing / on reports/ is optional but makes it clear you mean the directory, not a file named 'reports'.

faq.q: How do I rename a directory?
faq.a: mv old_name/ new_name/ — mv works for both files and directories. You don't need -r to rename (only to copy with cp -r). Example: mv my-project/ kernal-app/

examples: mkdir -p src/components src/pages src/utils is how you scaffold a new React project structure from the command line
rm -rf node_modules && npm install is the standard 'nuclear option' for fixing dependency issues
